title: Which jump size reaches both treasures?
description: Treasures sit on fourteen and thirty six. Listing the jump sizes for each treasure and keeping those on both lists shows which jump sizes reach both, and Keeko's doubt, that the size should be fourteen, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a jump size that reaches two numbers is in the list of each, and is called a common factor. Watch for students who pick the first treasure as the jump size.

source: Treasures are on 14 and 36 and Jumpy chooses jump size 7. He
video_script.why: The child lists the jump sizes that reach each treasure and keeps those on both lists, meeting the name common factor.
video_script.substitution: Write the jump sizes for each number and keep those that appear in both lists.
video_script.anchor: the treasure game of the book: {{NAME_4}} places treasures on fourteen and thirty six and {{NAME_2}} jumps with a size of seven
video_script.wrong_answer: the jump size should be fourteen
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the jump size should be fourteen, because fourteen is the first treasure. A jump of fourteen lands on fourteen, twenty eight and forty two, skipping thirty six, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The jump size should have been one or two

final_answer.value: 1 or 2; the common factors of 14 and 36
final_answer.spoken: the jump size should have been one or two

maths_rules: sizes that reach 6: 1, 2, 3, 6; sizes that reach 9: 1, 3, 9; on both lists: 1 and 3
on both lists: 1 and 2; 7 is on the first only

a jump size that reaches both numbers is called a common factor
video_script.design: One idea: the jump sizes on both lists reach both treasures, and they are the common factors. Assumes factors from the last video. Wrong idea: the first treasure is the jump size. The row stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the treasure game with two treasures.
<bookmark mark='place'/>{{NAME_4}} places treasures on fourteen and thirty six.
<bookmark mark='pick'/>{{NAME_2}} chooses a jump size of seven, starting from zero.
<bookmark mark='land'/>{{NAME_2}} lands on fourteen but not on thirty six.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What jump size should have been chosen?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two chests on 6 and 9; the jump sizes for 6 are 1, 2, 3, 6 and for 9 are 1, 3, 9; the sizes in both lists are 1 and 3

marks.nine: the list 1, 3, 9 is written under the chest on 9

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Take treasures on six and nine. The jump sizes that reach six are one, two, three and six.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>The jump sizes that reach nine are one, three and nine.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Only one and three are on both lists, so only they reach both treasures.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find a jump size that reaches both treasures.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: sizes that reach 14: 1, 2, 7, 14 (1 x 14, 2 x 7)
narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, list the jump sizes that reach fourteen. They are one, two, seven and fourteen.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>One times fourteen and two times seven make fourteen.

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step two, list the jump sizes that reach thirty six. They are one, two, three, four, six, nine, twelve, eighteen and thirty six.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: on both lists: 1 and 2; 7 is on the first list only

marks.seven: 7 is crossed out in the second list

narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step three, find the sizes on both lists. They are one and two.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Seven is on the first list but not on the second.

beats.on_screen: Check: 2 x 7 = 14 and 2 x 18 = 36; 7 goes to 35 and 42, so it misses 36

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step four, check a jump of two. Two times seven is fourteen, and two times eighteen is thirty six.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>A jump of seven goes to thirty five and then forty two, so it misses thirty six.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the jump size should have been 1 or 2; such a number is called a common factor

marks.name: the words common factor are written under the box

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The jump size should have been one or two.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A jump size that reaches both numbers is called a common factor.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the jump size should be fourteen.
<bookmark mark='why'/>That is because fourteen is the first treasure.
<bookmark mark='miss'/>But a jump of fourteen lands on fourteen, twenty eight and forty two, so it skips thirty six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A good jump size must reach both treasures, so the doubt is struck.
